question.text: A distributor in Jaipur (a B-30 city) brings in a new individual investor who invests Rs. 50,000 in an equity mutual fund through the Regular Plan. Per the current NISM V-A workbook framework, how does this transaction benefit the distributor compared with a similar transaction from Mumbai (a T-30 city)?

answer.text: The distributor earns double the trail commission for B-30 city investors
The distributor receives an additional Rs. 300 investor-borne transaction charge for B-30 city transactions
Under the revised framework, additional commission/incentives may be paid for onboarding new individual investors from B-30 cities (and for women investors), as specified by SEBI from time to time
B-30 city transactions are exempt from the prohibition on upfront commissions, so the distributor earns an upfront commission

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM V-A workbook describes a revised framework under which additional commission/incentives may be paid to distributors who onboard new individual investors from B-30 cities and women investors, as specified by SEBI from time to time. This replaces the older fixed "additional TER of 30 bps" framing for B-30 inflows. The Trap: Option A exaggerates by claiming a doubled trail. Option B invents an investor-borne transaction charge that has been withdrawn under the current framework. Option D is contrary to the uniform prohibition on upfront commissions. Cross-Exam Context: NISM V-A tests the revised framework alongside the withdrawal of investor-borne transaction charges. Chapter 5 also references B-30 incentives in TER regulation.
